goal: Make our links safer and faster.

functional.text: Create a short link for a long URL
acceptance: POST /api/urls returns 201 with a unique short code
Invalid or unsafe target URLs are rejected with 400
Creating the same URL again for the same client returns the existing link

functional.text: Redirect a short code to its target URL
acceptance: GET /{code} answers 302 with the target in Location

functional.text: Expose click analytics per short link
acceptance: GET /api/urls/{code}/stats returns total clicks, last access and a daily breakdown
Recording clicks never slows down redirects
A link created with expiresInMinutes stops redirecting after that time (410)
Out-of-range expiry values are rejected with 400
Requests above the per-client quota answer 429 with Retry-After
The quota window resets after it elapses

functional.text: Reject unsafe target URLs (non-http schemes, credentials, private/loopback networks)
acceptance: Loopback, private and link-local targets are rejected

assumptions: No end-user authentication in this iteration: clients are identified by the X-Client-Id header or IP (spoofable).
Single-instance deployment with in-memory storage behind a repository abstraction.
Stakeholder answer: "Block malicious and private-network target URLs and rate limit abusive clients; links must also support expiry."
Stakeholder answer: "p95 redirect latency under 50 ms at 500 req/s; click analytics must be recorded asynchronously."

clarificationsApplied.question: What does 'safer' mean here: which threats must be mitigated (malicious targets, abuse/spam, link tampering) and against which standard?
clarificationsApplied.answer: Block malicious and private-network target URLs and rate limit abusive clients; links must also support expiry.

clarificationsApplied.question: What latency target defines 'faster' (for example p95 redirect latency) and under what load?
clarificationsApplied.answer: p95 redirect latency under 50 ms at 500 req/s; click analytics must be recorded asynchronously.
